A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LeGrad with the same authors, core method and overlapping experiments. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation, open-vocabulary localization, perturbation and ablation results, including additional ImageNet-trained ViT experiments in the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds audio localization, inference-speed measurements, GradCAM controls, gradient-distribution analyses and FunnyBirds evaluation.

M1.justification: The attention-gradient computation, ReLU filtering, layer aggregation, normalization and attentional-pooler adaptation remain unchanged. v2 explicitly specifies token averaging and evaluates the existing procedure with ImageBind; these additions do not establish a revision to LeGrad's algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds sound- and speech-prompted localization on ADE20KSoundPrompted and ADE20KSpeechPrompted, PascalVOC for gradient-distribution analysis, and the synthetic, part-based FunnyBirds explanation benchmark. These substantially extend coverage beyond the retained ImageNet and OpenImages tasks.

E2.justification: The audio comparison introduces DAVENet, CAVMAE, ImageBind and DenseAV. Appendix Table 7 adds GradCAM without the CLS token and a multilayer GradCAM variant as evaluated controls. The main qualitative comparison also drops Rollout, although it remains in quantitative comparisons and appendix Figure 11.

E3.justification: New protocols include audio localization scored by mAP/mIoU, speed averaged over 1,000 images, mask-averaged and normalized layer-gradient analysis across pretrained weights, and FunnyBirds Co-12 evaluation. Table 2 also removes the BigG model configuration from OpenImages evaluation. Shared segmentation and perturbation settings retain their stated splits, thresholds and metrics.

E4.justification: v2 adds CLS-token and multilayer GradCAM controls, model- and class-specific gradient-distribution analyses, and a FunnyBirds sanity check. These investigate baseline adaptation, layer dependence and explanation quality. Existing layer-accumulation analyses remain; the ReLU/layer-aggregation ablation moves from v1 Table 5 to v2 appendix Table 9 without changed results.

E5.justification: v2 introduces shaded bands around gradient-profile curves in Figures 7, 9–10 and 12–18, but neither the text nor captions identify their statistic or construction. Their status as uncertainty estimates is therefore unclear. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds or formal significance testing.

E6.justification: Shared quantitative results match, but substantial new results appear. Table 5 reports sound mIoU of 38.9 for ImageBind + LeGrad versus DenseAV's 24.2, while speech mIoU is 21.8 versus 36.8. Table 3 reports LeGrad at 96 fps; Tables 7 and 10 add control and FunnyBirds scores. Table 2 removes all BigG results, including LeGrad's 36.47 p-mIoU.

T1.justification: v2 Section 3.2 explicitly defines the per-layer aggregated feature as the arithmetic mean of its tokens; v1 leaves that aggregation mathematically unspecified. Otherwise, the method and baseline equations are equivalent apart from notation and equation splitting. No theorem, proof or formal guarantee is added.

C1.justification: The introduction adds a specific claim of state-of-the-art zero-shot sound localization, advertised as approximately 14 mIoU above the previous best. The principal claims about attention gradients, multilayer aggregation, scalability and compatibility with different pooling mechanisms remain essentially unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of gradient profiles as model fingerprints, a training-frequency hypothesis for the person class, and explanations involving GradCAM activation ranges and computational speed. It also attributes limited speech improvements to ImageBind's training coverage. Conversely, v1's specific last-40%-of-layers recommendation and discussion of unresolved TextSpan/GradCAM artifacts disappear.

D1.justification: v2 adds pretrained-weight sources for new analyses, GradCAM adaptation details and a FunnyBirds framework link. However, it removes LeGrad's code/demo links and the explicit 224×224 input-resolution and no-fine-tuning statements. Most existing checkpoint identifiers and baseline implementation details remain. Removed links do not establish that the resources themselves became unavailable.

R1.justification: v2 adds positioning against audio-visual methods and references for ImageBind, DenseAV, CAVMAE, DAVENet, FunnyBirds, Co-12 and MetaCLIP. It removes the dedicated explanation-evaluation discussion and much of its faithfulness literature, including Saliency Cards and saliency sanity checks. It also removes the contrast claiming LeGrad is class-agnostic unlike CheferCAM.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative changes from shared settings followed by combined comparisons to task-specific subsections. Related work and qualitative discussion are substantially condensed, layer-wise qualitative interpretation is integrated into the ablation discussion, and the ReLU ablation moves to the appendix. Numerous existing passages and headings are rewritten.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column format to two columns, with extensive rearrangement of tables and figures. v2 adds speed, audio, GradCAM-control and FunnyBirds tables plus gradient-profile figures. Figure 6 is transposed and reduced to three examples, and Table 2 loses its BigG column. Existing appendix illustrations and the ReLU table are relocated.

improvement.justification: The GradCAM controls strengthen the comparative evidence, while gradient analyses, FunnyBirds evaluation and audio experiments better support layer aggregation and versatility. These are useful gains beyond merely adding scores. However, v2 removes code/demo and input-resolution information, omits the BigG OpenImages comparison, and leaves new timing settings and plot bands insufficiently explained. The resulting net improvement is positive but limited.
